rows.theme: Complaint about one kind of food; desire for vegetables and Egyptian foods

candidates.similarity: Both narrate Israelite discontent with food in the wilderness and mention Egyptian food, including cucumbers, onions, and garlic.
candidates.difference: Numbers names fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic and complains about manna; Q2:61 names herbs/greens, cucumbers, garlic or grain, lentils and onions and records Moses' reply. Lentils are not listed in Numbers 11:5, and the Hebrew has no exact equivalent of every Qur'anic food.

rows.caveat: Preliminary screening does not establish absence of older traditions or justify a verified Sources card.

rows.theme: Moses commands Israelites to slaughter a cow

candidates.relation: possible cow/heifer ritual-law contrast, not same event
candidates.similarity: Both passages concern a divinely specified bovine animal and ritual compliance.
candidates.difference: Numbers 19 prescribes a red, unblemished heifer not subjected to a yoke for purification from corpse impurity. Qur'an 2:67–70 recounts Moses and a questioned command to slaughter a cow, specifies middle age and vivid yellow color; neither narrative context nor color matches. Do not claim identical law or direct textual dependence.

rows.caveat: Preliminary screening does not establish absence of older traditions or justify a verified Sources card.
